info.title: Lumabill API
info.description:
The Lumabill API gives **Pro and Lifetime** subscribers programmatic access to
Swiss invoicing and bookkeeping data. You can create and manage invoices,
clients, expenses, journal entries, and more - the same data you see in the
Lumabill dashboard.

## Authentication

All requests must carry a Bearer API key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer lmb_your_api_key_here
```

API keys are created in **Settings → API Keys** inside the Lumabill dashboard.

## Profile scoping

A Lumabill account can have multiple profiles (companies). By default the key
is scoped to the profile it was created for. If a key has access to multiple
profiles, supply the `X-Profile-Id` header with the UUID of the target profile.

## Rate limits

| Operation | Limit |
|-----------|-------|
| Reads (GET) | 60 requests / minute per API key |
| Writes (POST, PUT, DELETE) | 20 requests / minute per API key |

When the limit is exceeded the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a
`Retry-After` header indicating when you may retry (seconds from now).

## Pagination

List endpoints support cursor-free page-based pagination via query parameters:

| Parameter | Default | Maximum |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `page` | 1 | - |
| `per_page` | 50 | 100 |

Responses include a top-level `meta` object:

```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": { "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total": 243 }
}
```

## Errors

All error responses share a common shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
    "message": "Human-readable description"
  }
}
```

Common error codes: `INVALID_API_KEY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`,
`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED`,
`READ_ONLY_KEY`, `CLIENT_NOT_FOUND`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Smart defaults

When creating invoices or offers the API auto-resolves most fields from
your profile so you can send minimal payloads. Only `lines` is required.

| Field | Auto-resolved from |
|-------|-------------------|
| `invoice_number` | Profile prefix + sequential counter (e.g. `IV-010`) |
| `issue_date` | Today |
| `due_date` | `issue_date` + profile payment deadline (default 30 days) |
| `currency` | Profile default currency (default `CHF`) |
| `vat_rate` (on lines) | Profile default tax rate |
| Sender details | Profile company name, address, IBAN, etc. |
| Payment info | Profile payment template and deadline |

**`client_id` shorthand** - pass a `client_id` UUID instead of a full
client object. The API fetches the client and snapshots the data
automatically. Returns `404` with code `CLIENT_NOT_FOUND` if the client
does not exist in your profile.

**Minimal example:**

```json
POST /invoices
{
  "client_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "lines": [
    { "description": "Consulting", "quantity": 2, "price": 150 }
  ]
}
```

Any field you explicitly provide overrides the auto-resolved default.

## MCP Server (AI Assistant Integration)

Connect your Lumabill account to AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor
using the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

**Endpoint:** `https://mcp.lumabill.ch/mcp?key={your_api_key}`

**Setup for Claude Desktop** - add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lumabill": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.lumabill.ch/mcp?key=lmb_your_key_here"
    }
  }
}
```

**Setup for Claude Code** - add to `.mcp.json` in your project:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lumabill": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.lumabill.ch/mcp?key=lmb_your_key_here"
    }
  }
}
```

**Setup for Cursor** - add to MCP settings:
- Name: `lumabill`
- Type: `streamable-http`
- URL: `https://mcp.lumabill.ch/mcp?key=lmb_your_key_here`

The MCP server exposes all API endpoints as tools. Your AI assistant can:
- Create and manage invoices, offers, and expenses
- Look up clients and vendors
- Generate financial reports (P&L, balance sheet, VAT)
- Import bank transactions
- Query revenue data

**API key permissions apply:** Read-only keys only expose read tools.
Same rate limits as the REST API (60 reads/min, 20 writes/min).

parameters.name: document_type
parameters.description: `invoice` (default): sales only. `credit_note`: credit notes (Gutschriften, negative totals). `all`: both.

put.description: Partial update: fields omitted from the body keep their stored values (invoice number, dates, client, sender, payment, currency, attachments, ...). Only invoices in `draft` status can be fully updated. Changing the `status` field moves the invoice through its lifecycle; status values are case-insensitive.

delete.description: Only draft invoices may be deleted.

get.summary: List the recorded payments of an invoice

post.description: Undoes one payment (by `paymentId`, else the most recent). The payment journal entry is reversed with a Storno on the payment date (nothing is deleted, the Buchungsnummer series stays gap-free), bank matches are released and the payment status is recomputed. Rejected with 400 `FISCAL_YEAR_CLOSED` when the payment date lies in a closed fiscal year.

post.summary: Create a credit note (Gutschrift) for an issued invoice
post.description: Creates a credit note linked to the invoice, in the profile's credit note number series, with the invoice's client, currency and VAT settings. Without `items` it credits the whole invoice (every line with its quantity negated). `issue: true` issues it right away: in double-entry mode revenue, receivable and output VAT are reversed on the credit note date, which is also the VAT period of the correction. `settle: true` (implies issue) sets it off against the invoice's open amount; `issue` + `settle` on a full credit cancels the invoice in one step. An invoice can no longer be issued with a negative total: this is the way to correct one.

items.description: Credited lines with NEGATIVE quantities (default - the invoice's lines negated)

invoiceNumber.description: null for a draft credit note (numbered in the credit note series when issued)

get.summary: List credit note settlements of an invoice or credit note

post.summary: Settle a credit note against open invoices (Verrechnung)
post.description: `{id}` is an issued credit note. Each allocation sets part of its credit off against an issued invoice of the same client and currency. No money moves and no journal entry is posted (the receivable already nets out); both documents' payment status is recomputed. An omitted amount takes as much as both sides allow, in list order. The date must lie in an open fiscal year.

200.description: Settlement removed; both documents are open again by its amount

post.summary: Get the public share link for an invoice or offer
post.description:
Returns the recipient-facing view URL for an invoice or an offer - the same link the send mail contains. Use it to hand someone a payment or viewing link without sending mail from Lumabill.

POST because the first call mints and persists the public token. It is idempotent: a document that already carries a token keeps it, so the URL stays stable once shared. Works for offers too, since offers are stored alongside invoices. A draft is rejected (400): the link would expose an unfinished document with no login and no expiry. Profile-scoped like GET /invoices/{id}.

url.description: Public view page for the document

paymentLink.description: Stripe checkout URL when online payment is configured on the document, otherwise null.

onlinePayment.description: Whether online payment is enabled on the document

post.description: Undoes one payment (by `paymentId`, else the most recent). The payment journal entry is reversed with a Storno on the payment date (nothing is deleted, the Buchungsnummer series stays gap-free), bank matches are released and the payment status is recomputed. Rejected with 400 `FISCAL_YEAR_CLOSED` when the payment date lies in a closed fiscal year.

get.description: Returns the profile's chart of accounts (Swiss Kontenplan KMU) with account UUIDs, codes, names and types. Account UUIDs are required for bank transaction adjustments, categorization, expense lines, and expense payments.

parameters.name: includeBalances
parameters.description: Include the current balance per account

parameters.name: fiscalYearId
parameters.description: Restrict balances to a fiscal year (with includeBalances=true)

post.summary: Add an account to the chart of accounts
post.description: Adds a custom account to the profile's Kontenplan, e.g. a liability account the default chart lacks (2270 Geschuldete Sozialversicherungen). The 4-digit code must match the type per Swiss Kontenrahmen KMU: 1xxx ASSET, 2000-2799 LIABILITY, 2800-2999 EQUITY, 3xxx REVENUE, 4xxx-7xxx EXPENSE. Codes are unique per profile. Permission `bookkeeping.create`; needs a read-write key.

409.description: The code already exists for this profile (`DUPLICATE_ACCOUNT_CODE`)

put.summary: Rename, regroup or deactivate a chart account
put.description: Code and type are fixed once created. Deactivating (`isActive: false`) is refused for system accounts (`ACCOUNT_IS_SYSTEM`) and for accounts that still carry a balance (`ACCOUNT_HAS_BALANCE`). Permission `bookkeeping.update`.

delete.description: Only accounts without journal lines can be deleted; otherwise the API answers 400 `ACCOUNT_HAS_ENTRIES`. System accounts are refused. Deactivate those via PUT instead. Permission `bookkeeping.delete`.

get.description: A Storno carries `isReversal: true` and `reversedEntryId`; the entry it reverses carries `reversedById` / `reversedBySeq`. With `includeVoided=true` the list also returns entries removed before Storno bookings existed that still hold a Buchungsnummer, marked with `deletedAt` and `voidReason`; they never count toward any balance.

200.description: A paginated list of journal entries

post.description: Debits and credits across all lines must balance (sum of debits = sum of credits). Mutations to entries in closed fiscal years are rejected.

put.description: Mutations to entries in closed fiscal years are rejected with `403`.

delete.summary: Withdraw a manual journal entry (posts a Storno)
delete.description: Posted bookings are never removed. Deleting a MANUAL entry posts a Storno, exactly like `POST /journal-entries/{id}/reverse`: a new numbered entry on the same date with debit and credit swapped, linked to the original. Errors (400 with `errorCode`): `NOT_MANUAL` (undo automatic bookings through their invoice, expense, payment or bank transaction), `ALREADY_REVERSED`, `IS_REVERSAL`, `FISCAL_YEAR_CLOSED`.

post.description: Posts a Storno for a MANUAL entry: a new numbered entry on the original's date with debit and credit swapped, linked via `reversedEntryId`. The original stays in the journal. An entry can be reversed once; its fiscal year must be open. Errors (400 with `errorCode`): `NOT_MANUAL`, `ALREADY_REVERSED`, `IS_REVERSAL`, `FISCAL_YEAR_CLOSED`.

delete.description: Removes the import and all of its transactions. Posted journal entries are soft-deleted (GeBüV-compliant audit trail) and any matched invoices, expenses, or revenues are reverted to their previous state.

put.description: Update a transaction's reconciliation state. Setting `status=MATCHED` with one or more invoices, an expense or a revenue posts the corresponding payment journal entries (one per invoice). Setting it back to `UNMATCHED` or `IGNORED` reverses all of them. Setting `status=CATEGORIZED` with `bookToAccountId` posts a direct booking against the chosen chart-of-accounts account. Optional `adjustments` book bank fees / rounding alongside the main entry. Mutations on transactions whose journal date falls in a closed fiscal year are rejected.

post.summary: Record a payment against an invoice
post.description: Marks an invoice as paid (fully or partially) and posts the payment journal entry when bookkeeping is on. Undo with `POST /invoices/{id}/unpay`.

get.summary: List profiles accessible to this API key

put.description: Partial update: only the fields sent change. Company and address fields feed the sender block of new documents; the `*NumberPrefix` and `*Count` fields drive numbering (`count` is the last number handed out). `baseCurrency` cannot change once journal entries exist (400). A key pinned to another profile, or a request scoped via `X-Profile-Id` to another profile, gets 404. Permission `profiles.update`; needs a read-write key.

get.summary: Get the account behind this API key
get.description:
Returns billing and plan info for the account: subscription state,
plan type, enabled modules, AI quota, locale, and login email.

The account is the user/billing layer (one Cognito identity, one
Stripe customer). Profiles are company-scoped and live under the
account - see `/profiles` for that data.

invoice_number.description: Explicit number (imports, own numbering schemes), stored as given also on a draft; 409 DUPLICATE_INVOICE_NUMBER when another document of the same type in the profile already uses it. If omitted, a draft stays unnumbered and the next number from the profile prefix + counter (e.g. `IV-010`) is assigned when the document is issued (status leaves draft, or it is emailed). null clears the number of a never-issued draft; an issued document keeps its number.

due_date.description: Defaults to `issue_date` + profile payment deadline days (default 30) if omitted.

lines.description: Full replacement line items (update only). Required when changing amount or vat_rate so the recognition journal entry can be rebuilt; the expense total becomes the sum of line amounts.

BankAccountWrite.description: On PUT, include `id` in the body. All fields other than `id` are optional on PUT.

chartAccountId.description: Linked chart-of-accounts posting account used when booking this bank account's transactions.

confirmPostingAccountChange.description: PUT only. Must be true to change `chartAccountId` when the bank account already has booked transactions; otherwise the request is rejected with 409 POSTING_ACCOUNT_HAS_BOOKINGS. Existing bookings stay on the old account; only new bookings use the new one.

transactions_count.description: Number of transactions parsed from the uploaded file

format.description: Source of the import - CAMT053, CAMT054, CSV, REVOLUT or PDF (AI-read PDF statement)

matchedCount.description: Transactions auto-matched or manually matched to invoices/expenses/revenues

categorizedCount.description: Transactions booked directly to a chart-of-accounts account

ignoredCount.description: Transactions explicitly skipped (will not produce a journal entry)

amount.description: Always positive; use `direction` to know if it is a credit or debit

matchedInvoices.description: Every invoice this bank transaction paid, in allocation order (multi-invoice match / Sammelzahlung). Empty when nothing is booked, including auto-match suggestions that only set matchedInvoiceId. matchedInvoiceId / matchedInvoiceNumber / matchedInvoiceStatus describe the first entry.

amount.description: Payment amount allocated to this invoice

matchedExpenses.description: Every expense this (debit) bank transaction paid, in allocation order (multi-expense match / Sammelzahlung). Empty when no expense is booked. matchedExpenseId / matchedExpenseVendor / matchedExpenseDescription describe the first entry.

amount.description: Payment amount allocated to this expense

adjustments.description: Bank fees, rounding, partial-payment splits booked alongside the main entry

journalEntryId.description: Posted journal entry, present once the transaction is reconciled

amount.description: Signed. Positive books a DEBIT (bank fee, Skonto, FX loss), negative a CREDIT (FX gain, overpayment). Must not be zero.

BankTransactionUpdate.description: Reconcile a single bank transaction. Setting `status=MATCHED` requires one of `matchedInvoiceIds` (or the legacy `matchedInvoiceId`), `matchedExpenseIds` (or the legacy `matchedExpenseId`), or `matchedRevenueId`. One bank payment can settle several invoices: the bank amount plus adjustments is allocated in the order of `matchedInvoiceIds`, each invoice getting min(open balance, money left), so only the last one can end partially paid. Errors (400): PAYMENT_EXCEEDS_OPEN_BALANCE (more money than the combined open balance), INVOICE_ALLOCATION_ZERO (an invoice would receive nothing), ADJUSTMENTS_EXCEED_ALLOCATION (adjustments are booked on the largest allocation and must be smaller than it), DUPLICATE_INVOICE, INVALID_MATCHED_INVOICES (both fields sent, or not 1-50 UUIDs). One DEBIT bank transaction can likewise pay several expenses (`matchedExpenseIds`, same rule; invoices only match CREDIT lines, expenses only DEBIT lines). An expense payment credits the bank with its allocation plus the signed adjustments, so positive adjustments (bank fees) are paid on top and negative ones (FX gain) reduce the bank amount. Expense-side codes: EXPENSE_ALLOCATION_ZERO, DUPLICATE_EXPENSE, INVALID_MATCHED_EXPENSES, ADJUSTMENTS_EXCEED_BANK_AMOUNT. Every journal entry of a group gets the bank date and a description starting with "Sammelzahlung" plus the bank reference. Undo a group by setting the transaction back to UNMATCHED; undoing one of its documents is refused with 409 (PAYMENT_IN_BANK_GROUP_MATCH / EXPENSE_PAYMENT_IN_BANK_GROUP_MATCH). Setting `status=CATEGORIZED` requires `bookToAccountId`. The journal entry is posted automatically and rejected if the affected fiscal year is closed.

matchedInvoiceId.description: Legacy single-invoice match, treated as `matchedInvoiceIds = [id]`. Do not send together with `matchedInvoiceIds`.

matchedInvoiceIds.description: Invoices paid by this bank transaction, in allocation order.

matchedExpenseId.description: Legacy single-expense match, treated as `matchedExpenseIds = [id]`. Do not send together with `matchedExpenseIds`.

matchedExpenseIds.description: Expenses paid by this DEBIT bank transaction, in allocation order.

paymentAccountId.description: Chart-of-accounts UUID of the receiving account (e.g. 1020 Bank). Required when bookkeeping is on (simple or double mode).

amount.description: Partial payment amount; omit to pay the remaining balance

CreditAllocation.description: A credit note set off against an invoice (Verrechnung)

PaymentRecord.description: One recorded payment of an invoice or expense (payment_history).

id.description: Pass as `paymentId` to the unpay endpoints to undo this payment

paymentId.description: Payment to undo (from the payments list); omit to undo the most recent payment

description.example: Revenue and expense summary for a given period.

data.description: Report payload. Structure varies by report type. Typical top-level keys: `sections` (array of named groups), `totals`.

Account.description:
The account is the user/billing layer (Cognito identity, Stripe customer,
plan, modules, AI quota). Distinct from a `Profile`, which holds
company-scoped invoicing data.

Profile.description: camelCase, as the API returns it (the earlier snake_case description of this schema never matched the response). Read endpoints also merge the account's subscription fields (plan, status) into the object.

iban.description: IBAN of the default currency slot in `currencyDefaults`

currencyDefaults.description: Per-currency IBAN, payment template and QR preference, keyed by currency code

invoiceCount.description: Last invoice number handed out; the next invoice gets count + 1

ProfileUpdate.description: Partial update for PUT /profiles/{id}. Every property is optional; anything omitted stays as is. Same keys as `Profile` minus the read-only ones (`id`, `isDefault`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`).

baseCurrency.description: Rejected with 400 once journal entries exist
